clue.text: Moved camp?

definitions.meaning: moved in the sense of emotionally stirred or touched
camp in the sense of mannered, theatrical, putting on a show

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the word: stirred emotionally, and also pretentious or artificial in manner.

clue.text: Peloponnesian city taking a year to build a ship

parts.note: Argos is an ancient city in the Peloponnese
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek city lays in a year's supplies to build a new ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An argosy is a large merchant ship, originally one from Ragusa, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: 22 may be found in this river vessel

parts.note: crossword convention: a river is something that flows, a flow-er
a pot is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: Something from clue 22 might be spotted aboard a boat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River vessel' reads as a boat, but 'river' gives FLOWER (a thing that flows) and 'vessel' gives POT. The definition points to the answer of 22-down, a flower grown in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchids and other plants are grown in a pot of this kind, so the 22-down answer may be found in one.

clue.text: Boxes unpopular at concerts, do we hear?

indicators.note: a question asking whether we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: people who cough during a performance are disliked by the audience

explanation.surface: A grumble that private boxes at concerts are unpopular, phrased as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: COUGHERS, people coughing at concerts, sounds like the plural of a word for strongboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are chests or strongboxes for keeping money and valuables.

clue.text: Number identified by woman finally changing sides

indicators.note: the last letter swaps one side for the other, left becoming right

parts.note: Ethel is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A figure is pinned down by a woman who at the last moment switches allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, but read it as 'numb-er', something that numbs. ETHEL ends in L (left); change it to R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was used as an anaesthetic, so it is a thing that deadens feeling, a numbing agent.

clue.text: Superior ranking of works of art out east

indicators.note: out says a letter is dropped from the word for the works of art

parts.note: statues are sculpted works of art
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A gallery's best-ranked works of art have been sent out east.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or prestige, a high position relative to others.

clue.text: Duets composed extremely adeptly in twenty-four hours

indicators.note: composed suggests the letters of the musical word are put together afresh
extremely asks for the extremities, the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Duets written with great skill in the space of a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges DUETS into TUESD; 'extremely' takes AY from the first and last letters of adeptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuesday is one day of the week, a span of twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Argument to note across the border

indicators.note: across means the note spreads over and around the other word

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A dispute over a musical note on the far side of the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts TE outside HEM, giving T + HEM + E. 'the border' sounds like a frontier but is only HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument can be the subject or main idea of a piece of writing, which is what a theme is.

clue.text: Aunt Sally's airs are manifest

definitions.note: read as Aunt Sally is: the 's is the verb

parts.note: side is pretentiousness, putting on airs, so airs means sides
to show is to make manifest

explanation.surface: A relative called Sally makes her pretensions plain for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing sticks at a dummy head; 'Aunt Sally's' means Aunt Sally is. To put on side is British slang for putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sally is a fairground attraction, a minor booth set apart from the main entertainment.

clue.text: Legal right of a poet to suppress verse

indicators.note: to suppress here means to hold down within, so the poet holds the verse inside

parts.note: Ernest Dowson was an English poet of the 1890s

explanation.surface: A legal entitlement allows a poet to censor some verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suppress' puts V inside DOWSON, giving DVOWSON after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Advowson is the English legal right to nominate a priest to a church living, a church-patronage entitlement.

clue.text: React angrily and blow up part of the pool

parts.note: to go off is to explode
the deep end is the part of a swimming pool where the water is deepest

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and wrecks a section of the swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper suddenly and violently.

clue.text: Kodiak may be her base

indicators.note: may be suggests these letters could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A large Alaskan bear may make its home here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges HER BASE. A Kodiak is a large brown bear from Alaska; the definition is by example, as one could be female.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kodiak is a huge Alaskan brown bear, and a female one is a sow of that species.

clue.text: The abnormality associated with one

parts.note: one is the first odd number, so the peculiar quality linked to it is its being odd rather than even

explanation.definitionFit: Unusualness or strangeness is the quality of being peculiar, and one is an odd number.

clue.text: Lyric poems about one's affairs

indicators.note: about means the poems go round the other piece

parts.note: epodes are lyric poems in which a long line is followed by a shorter one
one's read as one is gives I + S

explanation.surface: A poet writes lyric verse about their own love affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; the 's of 'one's' is read as 'is'. An epode is a classical lyric form, as written by Horace.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are incidents or happenings, as are affairs in the sense of events.

clue.text: Old car in teacher's control

indicators.note: in says the old car sits inside the teacher

parts.note: a don is a university teacher; the 's is the link is
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: An ancient motor parked inside a teacher's area of authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal: the old car goes inside the teacher, splitting him after his first letter. Don is the British word for a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereignty or authority, power to rule over something.

clue.text: Crude person after dance replaced spectacles

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of the dance are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance with interweaving figures
two round lenses look like the letters O O

explanation.surface: A boor who, after dancing, swapped his glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges HAY into YAH, and spectacles are pictured as OO. The hay is an English folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, brutish lout, after the beastly humans in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: An air-to ground missile used in the cold war?

definitions.text: An air-to ground missile used in the cold war?

parts.words: An air-to ground missile used in the cold war?
parts.note: military jargon recast as weather: a pellet of ice falling from the sky in a cold-weather onslaught

explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice falls from the sky to earth in cold weather, like a projectile dropped from the air.

clue.text: Schwanda's old woman — one decorating a cake

definitions.note: read as Schwanda is: the 's is the verb

parts.note: bag is a disparaging word for an old woman
a piper squeezes icing through a nozzle to decorate a cake

explanation.surface: A character's elderly wife spends her time icing a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Schwanda the Bagpiper is a Czech opera by Jaromir Weinberger; 'Schwanda's' means Schwanda is.
explanation.definitionFit: Schwanda is the title character of the opera, a musician who plays the pipes.

clue.text: Character taking wine in a church

indicators.note: taking means a church holds the wine inside it

parts.note: A plus CH, the abbreviation for church
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink of communion wine in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is the container signal. 'Character' suggests a person, but it means a letter, and the answer is how the letter H is spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the name of the letter H, and a letter is a character of the alphabet.

clue.text: Devise it, say, for chopping wood .

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: to hatch something is to devise it, so devise it is hatch it

explanation.surface: Plan it out, as one might say, before cutting firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a small axe, a hand tool used to split logs.

clue.text: Reclusive as Scotsman starting with a twitch

indicators.note: starting with puts the Scotsman at the front of the rest

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of man
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is a hermit after developing a nervous twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting with' puts MON first, then AS and TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Monastic life is secluded and withdrawn from the world, like a monk's.

clue.text: Cover for a novel about passion

indicators.note: about means the novel goes round the passion

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
heat is intensity of passion

explanation.surface: A dust jacket for a romantic novel full of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. Haggard's She, the story of an immortal queen, is a crossword favourite for these three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a blade is to put a cover over it, encase it.

clue.text: Soldiers rebuked for one of Miss Blandish's deficiencies

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: Troops are scolded for what a lady called Miss Blandish lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the 1939 crime novel No Orchids for Miss Blandish by James Hadley Chase.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's title says she has none of these flowers, so each is one of the things she lacks.

clue.text: Vessels missing in battle for a Lancashire town

indicators.note: missing says the vessels are absent from the battle's name

parts.note: Prestonpans was a 1745 battle near Edinburgh in the Jacobite rising
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: Ships lost in a battle fought for possession of a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships but means cooking pans. Preston is a town in Lancashire, a county of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire, long a town, in north-west England.

clue.text: Order cited freely

indicators.note: freely means the letters of the word are allowed to move about at will

explanation.surface: A command quoted loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is a decree, an official command issued by authority.

clue.text: Writer on board -a royal poet

parts.note: pen for a writer, put on board ship by sitting between S and S, the steamship abbreviation
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A writer aboard ship who is also a court poet.
explanation.walkthrough: SS (steamship) stands for a ship, so 'on board' puts PEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was an Elizabethan poet, author of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: In I Kings he bade farewell to a land of riches

indicators.note: In says the answer is held within the following words of the clue

explanation.surface: A biblical farewell in the First Book of Kings.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Kings he bade'. In 1 Kings 10 the Queen of Sheba visits Solomon bringing great riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was the ancient kingdom of the wealthy queen who brought Solomon gold and spices.

clue.text: Promise union trouble, others not being involved

parts.note: a plight is a difficult or troubled situation

indicators.note: being involved suggests these words are tangled together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A promise of union brings trouble because others refuse to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being involved' rearranges OTHERS NOT into ONESTROTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge one's word in marriage is to vow to wed, an old phrase for betrothal.

clue.text: Turner has to take King round gallery

parts.note: R, rex, is the abbreviation for king
O is round in shape
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: The painter Turner must take the King round the art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J. M. W. Turner, whose works hang in the Tate, but it is the definition: something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn, spin round, so a thing that does that is one that turns.

clue.text: It bought protection in many a fanciful legend

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, standing for many

indicators.note: fanciful suggests the letters are imagined in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An old legend tells of buying safety at a high price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fanciful' rearranges A + LEGEND into ANEGELD, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Danegeld was a tax paid to Danish raiders to buy them off, protection money.
